source.title: Deep Double Descent via Smooth Interpolation
source.authors: Matteo Gamba; Erik Englesson; Mårten Björkman; Hossein Azizpour

record.tranche_reason: The study sweeps deep-network size and training time and measures test error, reproducing model-wise and epoch-wise double descent in its own settings.
record.gate_note: The paper's main results concern input-space loss sharpness, not test error. Rows below include the reported test-error results that bear on the claim; many are shown only in figures. Mentioned double-descent results from other studies are not included.
record.test_reason: The study reproduces Nakkiran et al.'s ConvNet and ResNet18 width sweeps on CIFAR-10 with 20% label noise and on CIFAR-100, trained 4k epochs. It reports test error against model width and against epochs, the original method and measure. Its main contribution, input-space loss sharpness, is a different construct.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors find a strong correlation between model-wise and epoch-wise test-error double descent and input-space loss smoothness around training points. Overparameterization promotes smooth interpolation of both clean and noisy data, which aligns with better generalization only at low label-noise ratios. Large models confidently predict noisy targets over volumes around noisy points, contrary to the polynomial intuition.
record.recipe_differences: The authors say they follow Nakkiran et al.'s experimental setup for deep double descent, while adding input-space loss-landscape measurements and extending to other datasets and architectures.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported test-error behavior varies with architecture and dataset; for ResNet18s trained with augmentation, the test-error peak occurs earlier than the interpolation threshold. Under asymmetric label noise on CIFAR-100, the trend differs between test samples from corrupted and unperturbed classes.

fits_no_version.finding: Under asymmetric noise on CIFAR-100 (80% of labels in 20 classes corrupted), test-error double descent remains for unperturbed classes but disappears for corrupted classes.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Model-wise double descent in test error is carried by test samples from clean classes; it is absent for test samples from classes whose training labels were heavily corrupted.

fits_no_version.finding: Input-space loss sharpness (Jacobian and tangent Hessian norms, volume crossentropy) follows model-wise and epoch-wise double descent. This holds even with 100% noisy labels, where test error is at chance.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Input-space sharpness of the training loss peaks at the interpolation threshold and falls with overparameterization, regardless of whether generalization improves.

record.problems: The test-error results are presented in figures without exact values in the text. The study uses selected datasets and training conditions; the text notes limited fine-grained control over model size in the ResNet setting.
record.rows_left_out: No additional test-error results relevant to the listed versions were left out. The many input-space loss, Jacobian, and Hessian results were not entered as rows because they do not measure the test-error behavior named in the claim.

untested.parts: Only width sweeps of ConvNets, ResNet18s and small Transformers. The interpolation threshold is located only for ConvNets (w=15) and ResNets (w=18).
No epoch-wise test-error result for Transformers or for CIFAR-100.
Entire version; there is no sample-size sweep.
Entire version; only deep networks are trained (the polynomial example is an illustration).

Entire version. There is no noise-level sweep, no regularization sweep and no multiple-descent analysis. CIFAR-100 without added noise still shows double descent, which the authors attribute to dataset complexity.

missing.what: ConvNets with base width w<15 do not reduce test error within 4k epochs, so no epoch-wise double descent below the threshold.
ResNets trained on 100% noisy CIFAR-10 labels: test error stays near random chance across widths, so there is no test-error double descent.

record.verdict_notes: All test-error results are figure-only, with no numbers in the text. V6 is not tested: the reader's V6 rows (r8, r9) are a per-class-group decomposition, with no noise or regularization sweep. Neither original source is this study.

versions.untested_parts: The study tests model-wise test-error trends in the stated network and dataset settings, not all deep-network architectures or settings.
Epoch-wise test error is reported for ConvNets and ResNets; no epoch-wise test-error result is reported for the Transformer experiments.
No training-sample-size sweep testing whether more data raises test error near interpolation.
The experiments use deep networks; they do not test a general double-descent curve across model classes beyond deep networks.
No single effective-complexity measure is tested as predicting peak locations across size, epochs, and sample count.
The study compares selected label-corruption conditions but does not test variance as a mechanism, multiple or triple descent, or whether optimally tuned regularization removes the peak.
No re-counting of complexity by an effective number of parameters.
